newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to consolidate, trend still up.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to consolidate, trend still up.

text.p: Belgian shares ended half a percent lower on Thursday in the wake of the Dow Jones' .DJI plunge on Wednesday, but held up better than neighbouring Paris and Amsterdam markets as bargain hunters scooped up stocks.
Dealers felt the market needed a period of consolidation to digest the steep rise of the past months, adding that they had little doubt the uptrend was still intact.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended 13.41 points, or 0.54 percent, lower at 2,486.81.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere (UM) topped the volume chart with 1.4 billion francs worth of trade.

The shares closed 1.16 percent lower at 3,410 francs in the aftermath of the sale of 24 pct of the company's shares to institutional investors Wednesday. Trade in UM shares was worth half of the 2.88 billion franc volume in Bel-20 shares.

Cement maker CBR and chemical stock Solvay were hardest hit by profit-taking, each down more than two percent at 3,190 and 21,825 francs respectively. Several other blue-chips gave up more than one percent.
Pharmaceutical group UCB was the only share to buck the trend, rising by one percent to 128,800 francs.
